question: How long was the ark of the covenant at Abinadab's house?
summary: 1 Samuel 7:1-2 says the ark stayed at Abinadab's house in Kiriath-jearim for twenty years. The internal chronology of 1-2 Samuel — Samuel's judgeship, Saul's reign, and the early years of David's reign before he brought up the ark in 2 Samuel 6 — adds up to substantially more than twenty years, probably more than forty.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read the "twenty years" of 1 Samuel 7:2 not as the ark's whole stay but as the span until Israel's revival, leaving the full forty-plus years to run on to David.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells, who notes the ark reached Abinadab's house before Saul's reign yet stayed until David fetched it, a span the plain "twenty years" cannot cover.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: It could not be less than between forty and fifty years, for it remained here until the times of David, who removed it from hence after he was made king over all Israel, and when he had reigned over Judah seven years … for it was twenty years; not that this was all the time the ark was at Kirjathjearim, but it was so long there before it was much taken notice of, and sought unto, and the Lord by it …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill alone states both poles of the resolution: the ark's total stay was forty-to-fifty years (running until David's reign), and the "twenty years" of 7:2 measures only the period before Israel revived and sought the Lord, not the whole duration. Directly answers the 20-vs-40+ chronology tension. Two non-adjacent verbatim spans, sense-preserving ellipsis join; both truncated mid-sentence with the U+2026 marker.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And it came to pass, while the ark abode in Kirjathjearim, that the time was long,.... It could not be less than between forty and fifty years, for it remained here until the times of David, who removed it from hence after he was made king over all Israel, and when he had reigned over Judah seven years; and from the death of Eli to that time, which included the government of Samuel and Saul, it could not be less than what has been hinted:
for it was twenty years; not that this was all the time the ark was at Kirjathjearim, but it was so long there before it was much taken notice of, and sought unto, and the Lord by it; there was a great neglect of God, and his worship, which through the means of Samuel began to revive about this time, as it follows:
and all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord; became sensible of their evil doings, and repented of them, and sought the Lord with fasting, and prayer, and tears; bewailed their backslidings and revoltings from him, and cried after a departing God.
